questions.question: Normalizing is a process of heat treating _____.
questions.explanation:
Normalizing is a heat-treating process used on ferrous metals only. The steel is heated above its critical temperature range and then cooled in still air, which refines the grain structure and relieves internal stresses left by forging, casting, machining, or welding.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Non-ferrous metals aside from aluminum → Metals such as copper and magnesium alloys are annealed or stress-relieved; normalizing depends on iron-carbon transformations that they do not have.  
• Aluminum alloys only → Aluminum alloys are solution heat-treated, quenched, and aged (or annealed), never normalized.  
• Both ferrous and non-ferrous metals → Normalizing is limited to ferrous metals, so adding non-ferrous makes the statement wrong.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Normalizing → Ferrous only, air-cooled, refines grain.  
• Annealing → Softens the metal, slow furnace cooling.  
• Hardening → Heat and quench to increase hardness.  
• Tempering → Reheat after hardening to reduce brittleness.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Normalizing = Normal air cooling, for Iron (Fe) only.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Normalizing and annealing both heat the metal, but normalizing cools in open air (stronger, finer grain) while annealing cools slowly in the furnace (softer).

questions.question: What does an X on a cable indicate?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: AC power.

In the cable-identification convention used by this exam question, X indicates AC power. Control system is not the keyed meaning of X here. Aircraft cable markings should be interpreted using the aircraft wiring diagram and applicable manufacturer documentation.

questions.question: At what temperature should steel be tempered?
questions.explanation:
Tempering reheats hardened steel to a temperature below its critical (annealing) temperature and then cools it. Because the steel is not heated back into the critical range, it keeps most of its hardness while internal stresses and brittleness are reduced.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Above annealing temperature → Heating above the critical range re-austenitizes the steel, which undoes the hardening instead of toughening it.  
• At annealing temperature → That is the annealing cycle itself, which makes steel soft and removes the hardness you want to keep.  
• 1.5 times the annealing temperature → No such rule exists, and that temperature would be near melting and ruin the part.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Hardening → Heat above critical, then quench.  
• Tempering → Reheat below critical to reduce brittleness.  
• Annealing → Heat and cool slowly to soften.  
• Normalizing → Heat and air-cool to refine grain.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Temper = Tone it down (reheat below the critical temperature).  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Tempering always follows hardening, and it always trades a little hardness for extra toughness.

questions.question: If a material is found to be in the tertiary phase of creep, it _____.
choices: should be stop drilled and be condition-monitored
should undergo dye-penetrant inspection for evaluation
is still safe to be used
questions.explanation:
Creep is slow, permanent deformation under constant stress at high temperature. It has three phases, and the tertiary phase is the accelerating stage just before rupture. A part in tertiary creep is near failure and should be replaced immediately.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Stop drilled and condition-monitored → Stop drilling is a repair for cracks, and a part near creep rupture cannot be safely monitored.  
• Dye-penetrant inspection → Penetrant finds surface cracks, but tertiary creep already means the material is about to fail.  
• Still safe to be used → This describes the primary or secondary phases, not the tertiary.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Primary creep → Strain rate decreases.  
• Secondary creep → Steady, nearly constant strain rate.  
• Tertiary creep → Rapidly accelerating strain leading to rupture.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Tertiary = Terminal.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Creep matters most for turbine blades and other hot-section parts, where heat and sustained stress act together.

questions.question: Unless otherwise specified, torque values for tightening aircraft nuts and bolts relate to _____.
choices: both dry and lightly oiled threads
questions.explanation:
Standard torque values for aircraft nuts and bolts assume clean, dry threads unless the manufacturer says otherwise. Torque is only a way to measure bolt preload, and friction at the threads changes how much preload a given torque produces.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Clean, lightly-oiled threads → Lubrication lowers friction, so the same torque produces more preload and can overstress the bolt.  
• Clean, oil-soaked threads → Even more friction is removed, so the bolt would be badly over-tightened at the table value.  
• Both dry and lightly oiled threads → The tables are written for one thread condition, not two.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Dry threads → Table torque values apply.  
• Lubricated threads → Use a reduced torque only if the manufacturer specifies it.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Dry torque = default torque.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Always follow the maintenance manual first. If it specifies lubricated threads, use its value instead of the general table.

questions.question: Why is Nickel Chromium used in many exhaust systems?
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred, and option B is also arguable on pure material properties. Confirm the exact wording in your reference.  
  
Nickel-chromium alloys (such as Inconel) are used in exhaust systems because they resist corrosion and stay dimensionally stable at high temperature. Their low coefficient of thermal expansion helps limit warping and cracking as the exhaust heats and cools.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Lightweight and flexible → Nickel-chromium alloys are dense and fairly stiff, so they are chosen for heat resistance, not weight savings.  
• Corrosion-resistant and low heat conductivity → Low conductivity is plausible for these alloys, but the exam's intended pairing is corrosion resistance with low expansion.  
• Corrosion-resistant and high heat conductivity → Nickel-chromium alloys are poor heat conductors, so this is false.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Inconel → Nickel-chromium alloy for hot exhaust parts.  
• Stainless steel → Common exhaust material, less heat-tolerant than Inconel.  
• Titanium → Light and strong, used in some cooler exhaust areas.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Nickel + Chromium = Never Cracking when hot.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Think heat plus corrosion: hot-section parts are made of nickel-based alloys.

questions.question: How are pressure hoses categorized?
choices: According to the max allowable load
According to the max applied pressure
questions.explanation:
Hoses are sized by their inside diameter, which determines flow capacity. Hose size is usually written as a dash number in sixteenths of an inch of inside diameter.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Outer diameter → This is how rigid tubing is sized, not hose.  
• Max allowable load → Hoses are not classified by load.  
• Max applied pressure → Pressure rating is a separate specification (low, medium, high pressure), not the sizing category.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Tubing → Sized by outside diameter.  
• Hose → Sized by inside diameter.  
• Pressure rating → Separate classification of the hose.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Hose = Hole size (inside diameter).  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Tube = Outside, Hose = Inside. This pair shows up often.

questions.question: The dimensions of an MS20430AD8-6 rivets are _____.
choices: 3/8 inch in length and 1/4 inch in diameter
1/2 inch in length and 3/16 inch in diameter
1/4 inch in diameter and 3/8 inch in length
3/16 inch in diameter and 1/2 inch in length
questions.answerText: 1/4 inch in diameter and 3/8 inch in length
questions.explanation:
In MS20430AD8-6, the AD is the rivet material (2117-T4), the first number (8) is the diameter in 32nds of an inch, and the second number (6) is the length in 16ths of an inch. So the diameter is 8/32 = 1/4 inch and the length is 6/16 = 3/8 inch.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 3/8 inch in length and 1/4 inch in diameter → This has the same dimensions as the keyed answer. It looks like a duplicate in the source, so choose the keyed option (C).  
• 1/2 inch in length and 3/16 inch in diameter → That would be a 6-8 rivet (6/32 = 3/16 inch, 8/16 = 1/2 inch).  
• 3/16 inch in diameter and 1/2 inch in length → Same dimensions as the previous option, again a 6-8 rivet.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Diameter number → Thirty-seconds of an inch.  
• Length number → Sixteenths of an inch.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Diameter in 32nds, Length in 16ths.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Options A and C are identical in this file; decide by letter if you see this in practice. Always convert both numbers before looking at the choices.

questions.question: A category of plastic material that is capable of softening or flowing when reheated is described as a _____.
questions.explanation:
A thermoplastic softens and flows again when it is reheated, so it can be reshaped many times. Acrylic (Plexiglas) and nylon are common aircraft examples.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Thermocure → Not a standard plastics term.  
• Thermoset → Once cured, it permanently hardens and cannot be softened again (epoxy, polyester).  
• Thermoflow → Not a standard plastics term.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Thermoplastic → Re-softens with heat.  
• Thermoset → Cures permanently, does not re-soften.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Thermo-PLASTIC = Plastic again when heated.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Composite matrix resins such as epoxy are thermosets, which is why they cannot be reshaped after curing.

questions.question: The side clearances of piston rings are measure with a _____.
questions.explanation:
Piston ring side clearance is the gap between the ring and the groove land. It is checked by sliding a thickness (feeler) gauge between the ring and the land.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Dial gauge → Used for bore and runout checks, not for a thin gap in a ring groove.  
• Micrometer caliper gauge → Measures outside dimensions such as ring thickness, not clearance.  
• Protractor → Measures angles.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Side clearance → Feeler gauge between ring and land.  
• End gap → Feeler gauge with the ring squared in the cylinder.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Side gap = Slide a feeler.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Both ring side clearance and end gap use a feeler gauge, but the ring is positioned differently.

questions.question: A light aircraft is weighed in the flying position with the following weights recorded: left wheel is 800 lbs, right wheel is 810 lbs, and nose wheel is 150 lbs. The nosewheel is 12 inches behind the firewall (datum line). The distance between the main wheels and the nose wheel is 68 inches. The CG of the aircraft is located at _____.
choices: 5.8 inches ahead of the main wheels.
questions.answerText: 5.8 inches ahead of the main wheels.
questions.explanation:
Find the CG by taking moments about the main wheels. The nose wheel supports 150 lb at a distance of 68 inches from the mains, and the total weight is 800 + 810 + 150 = 1,760 lb.  
  
$$CG = \frac{F \times L}{W} = \frac{150 \times 68}{1{,}760} \approx 5.8\ \text{in}$$  
  
The CG is about 5.8 inches ahead of the main wheels. The mains are 12 + 68 = 80 inches aft of the datum, so the CG is about 74.2 inches aft of the firewall, which is not among the other choices.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 62.2 inches behind the firewall → This would put the CG far too far forward.  
• 73.2 inches behind the firewall → Close, but about 1 inch off the calculated 74.2 inches.  
• 75.2 inches behind the firewall → Close, but about 1 inch off the calculated 74.2 inches.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Moment → Weight × arm.  
• CG → Total moment ÷ total weight.  
• Nose-wheel method → Use nose weight, wheelbase, and total weight.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
CG from the mains = (Nose weight × Wheelbase) ÷ Total weight.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Add all three scale readings for total weight, and watch whether the distances are measured from the datum or from the mains.

questions.question: In what direction/s are composite fabric materials considered to be strongest?
questions.explanation:
In a woven fabric, the warp threads run lengthwise and are the straightest, so they carry the most load. The weft (fill) threads run across and have more crimp, so they are somewhat weaker.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• All → Fabrics are not equally strong in every direction.  
• Bias → Loads at 45° are carried mostly by the weave stretching, so this is the weakest direction.  
• Weft → Strong, but with more crimp and usually less strength than the warp.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Warp → Lengthwise, strongest.  
• Weft (fill) → Crosswise, less strong.  
• Bias → 45°, most stretch and drape, lowest strength.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
WARP = Wire-straight, strongest.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Always check fiber direction when laying up composite plies; strength depends on it.

questions.question: Why is steel tempered after being hardened?
choices: To increase its hardness and ductility.
To increase its strength and decrease its internal stresses.
To relieve its internal stresses and increase its brittleness.
To relieve its internal stresses and reduce its brittleness.
questions.answerText: To relieve its internal stresses and reduce its brittleness.
questions.explanation:
Hardened steel is very hard but brittle and contains internal stresses from quenching. Tempering reheats it to a controlled lower temperature to relieve those stresses and reduce brittleness, trading a small amount of hardness for toughness.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• To increase its hardness and ductility → Tempering slightly reduces hardness, and hardness and ductility do not rise together.  
• To increase its strength and decrease its internal stresses → Tempering mainly improves toughness; strength typically drops slightly.  
• To relieve its internal stresses and increase its brittleness → Tempering reduces brittleness; it never increases it.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Hardening → Raises hardness and brittleness.  
• Tempering → Reduces brittleness and stress.  
• Annealing → Makes the steel soft and ductile.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Temper = Tame the brittleness.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Look for the choice that says relieves stress and reduces brittleness; wrong choices usually reverse one of those two.

questions.question: What is the color code for fire-extinguisher lines?
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred, and the keyed answer (Red) conflicts with the standard code as I know it (brown for fire protection). Verify in AC 43.13-1B before relying on it.  
  
Fire-extinguisher (fire-protection) lines are identified with a brown color code in the standard line-identification chart.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Black → Not the code for fire-protection lines.  
• Red → Commonly used for fuel or other flammable fluid lines, not fire-extinguishing lines.  
• Yellow → Commonly used for lubricating oil lines.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Fire protection → Brown.  
• Fuel → Red.  
• Lubricating oil → Yellow.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Fire extinguisher = Brown, as in brown-out the flames.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Memorize the line-identification table as a group; fuel, oil, hydraulic, oxygen, and fire protection all have different colors.

questions.question: What is the color of an AN fitting?
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred, and I could not match Red to any standard AN fitting color. Please confirm against the source key.  
  
I can't confirm a red AN fitting from the standard references I know. AN fittings are normally identified by material: blue for aluminum alloy, and black or cadmium-plated for steel.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
AN fittings → Check the color against the material, not the fluid.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Check the source PDF for the exact wording and answer before studying this item.

questions.question: In Gas Tungsten Arc welding, a stream of inert gas is used to _____.
choices: attract oxygen to the puddle of molten metal
concentrate the heat of the arc and prevent its dissipation
lower the temperature required to properly fuse the metal
prevent the formation of oxides in the puddle
questions.answerText: prevent the formation of oxides in the puddle
questions.explanation:
In Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (TIG), a stream of inert gas such as argon or helium surrounds the arc and puddle. It keeps oxygen and nitrogen from the air away from the molten metal and the tungsten electrode, preventing oxides and contamination.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Attract oxygen to the puddle → The opposite of the gas's purpose.  
• Concentrate the heat of the arc and prevent its dissipation → The arc itself sets the heat concentration, not the shielding gas.  
• Lower the temperature required to properly fuse the metal → Shielding gas does not change the fusion temperature.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• GTAW → Tungsten electrode, inert shielding gas.  
• Oxy-acetylene → Flame plus flux or filler, no shielding gas.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Inert gas = Invisible shield.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
The gas protects the weld, not the filler rod. Inert means it does not react with the metal.

questions.question: A squib, as used in a fire-protection system, is a __ ___.
choices: device for causing the fire-extinguishing agent to be released
probe used for installing frangible disks in extinguisher bottles
questions.answerText: device for causing the fire-extinguishing agent to be released
questions.explanation:
A squib is a small explosive cartridge inside the discharge valve of a fire-extinguisher bottle. When it is fired electrically, it breaks the frangible disk and releases the extinguishing agent.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Probe for installing frangible disks → Not a tool; the squib is part of the bottle assembly.  
• Temperature-sensing device → That describes a fire detector.  
• Wizard-born muggle → A joke option, not a real answer.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Squib → Fires the extinguisher bottle.  
• Frangible disk → Seals the bottle until it ruptures.  
• Fire detector → Senses heat or flame.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Squib = Squirts the agent.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Squibs have a service life; check the cartridge date and keep a record for replacement.

questions.question: How should a welding torch flame be adjusted to weld stainless steel?
choices: Welding stainless steel is not acceptable for aircrafts.
questions.explanation:
A neutral oxy-acetylene flame (equal oxygen and acetylene) is used to weld stainless steel. It limits oxidation of chromium and avoids adding carbon, both of which hurt corrosion resistance.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Slightly carburizing → Extra carbon can form chromium carbides and reduce corrosion resistance.  
• Slightly oxidizing → Burns off chromium and makes the weld brittle and porous.  
• Welding stainless steel is not acceptable for aircraft → Incorrect; stainless steel is routinely welded on aircraft parts such as exhaust components.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Neutral flame → Balanced, used for most steels.  
• Carburizing flame → Excess acetylene.  
• Oxidizing flame → Excess oxygen.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Neutral flame = Neutral outcome, no added carbon or oxidation.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Know all three flame types and which metals prefer each.

questions.question: Which heat-treating operation would be performed when the surface of the metal is changed chemically by introducing a high carbide or nitride content?
questions.explanation:
Case hardening changes the chemistry of the metal's surface by adding carbon or nitrogen (carburizing, nitriding, cyaniding), creating a hard surface over a tougher core.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Welding → Joins metals; it is not a heat-treating operation that adds carbon or nitrogen to the surface.  
• Tempering → Reduces brittleness after hardening and does not change the surface chemistry.  
• Normalizing → Refines grain and relieves stress without changing the chemistry.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Case hardening → Hard surface, tough core.  
• Through hardening → Uniform hardness throughout.  
• Tempering → Reduces brittleness.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Case hardening = Carbon coat on the case.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Look for key words such as introducing carbon or nitrogen at the surface; they point to case hardening.

questions.question: [Question text not present in the answer key PDF]
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: The question text is missing in the source PDF. This explanation assumes it describes resistance to indentation, scratching, or abrasion, so confirm the wording.  
  
Hardness is a material's ability to resist localized surface deformation such as indentation, scratching, or abrasion. It is one of the primary properties evaluated during quality control of aircraft materials.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Toughness refers to the ability to absorb energy before fracture.  
• Ductility is the ability to deform plastically under tensile loading.  
• Fusibility is the ability of a metal to become liquid when heated and to join with other metals.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Hardness → Resists indentation.  
• Toughness → Resists fracture.  
• Ductility → Stretches before breaking.  
• Fusibility → Melts and fuses.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Hardness = Hard to dent.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Hardness and toughness are not synonymous. A very hard material may still fracture easily.

questions.question: The replacement of a damaged vertical stabilizer with a new identical stabilizer purchased from the aircraft manufacturer is considered a _____.
questions.explanation:
Replacing a damaged vertical stabilizer with an identical new part restores the aircraft to its original design, so it is a repair rather than an alteration. A vertical stabilizer is primary structure, so the repair is major.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Major alteration → An alteration changes the type design; an identical replacement does not.  
• Minor alteration → Same problem; this is not a design change.  
• Minor repair → Minor repairs are simple and do not affect structural strength or flight characteristics. Replacing a primary structure does.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Repair → Returns to the original condition.  
• Alteration → Changes the original design.  
• Major → Affects structure, weight, balance, or flight characteristics.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Same part back = Repair; different part = Alteration.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Major repairs and alterations are recorded on FAA Form 337. Minor repairs are not.

questions.question: What is likely to occur if hydrated wash primer is applied to unpainted aluminum and then about 30 to 40 minutes later afinish topcoat, when the humidity is low?
choices: Reflection of ultraviolet from the fabric
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred and one option is blank in the source. Confirm the exact question wording before relying on it.  
  
Blushing (a milky, dull finish) happens when moisture condenses in a drying coat, which is a problem in high humidity. In low humidity, a topcoat applied about 30 to 40 minutes after the wash primer should dry to a glossy, blush-free finish.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Option B → The text is missing in the source file.  
• Corrosion → Wash primer provides corrosion protection; the topcoat timing here does not cause corrosion.  
• Reflection of ultraviolet from the fabric → Unrelated to wash primer and topcoat on aluminum.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Blushing → High humidity, moisture trapped in the finish.  
• Runs and sags → Too much material in one coat.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Low humidity = No blush.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Humidity and temperature control how finishes behave; know the typical defects and their causes.

questions.question: [Question text partially missing in the answer key PDF] An aircraft had an empty weight of 2,886 lb with a moment of 101,673.78 in-lb before several alterations were made. The alterations included: removing two passenger seats (45 lb [alteration details missing in source] alterations caused the new empty weight to move _____.
choices: 36.6 inches aft of the original empty weight CG
2.81 inches aft of the original empty weigh CG
1.40 inches aft of the original empty weight CG
1.88 inches aft of the original empty weight CG
questions.answerText: 1.88 inches aft of the original empty weight CG
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: Part of the question is missing in the source (alteration details), so I could not re-derive the 1.88 inches. The highlighted answer comes from the source key.  
  
To find how alterations shift the empty-weight CG, update the weight and moment totals and recompute the CG.  
  
$$CG = \frac{\text{Total moment}}{\text{Total weight}}$$  
  
$$CG_{\text{original}} = \frac{101{,}673.78}{2{,}886} \approx 35.23\ \text{in}$$  
  
$$\Delta CG = CG_{\text{new}} - CG_{\text{original}}$$  
  
The source highlights 1.88 inches aft of the original empty-weight CG as correct.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Other choices → They are distractors; they cannot be checked here because the alteration details are missing in the source.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Items removed → Subtract their weight and moment.  
• Items added → Add their weight and moment.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Remove, add, then divide: new CG = new moment ÷ new weight.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Removed items subtract their weight and moment; added items add them. A positive answer means the CG moved aft.

questions.question: The most important consideration when selecting welding rod is ______.
questions.explanation:
The filler rod must be compatible with the base metal so the weld has the right strength, composition, and corrosion resistance. Material compatibility is the most important consideration when choosing a welding rod.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Ambient conditions → Affect technique, but they do not decide which rod to use.  
• Amount of acetylene → A gas supply setting, unrelated to choosing a rod.  
• Flame temperature → Set by the gas mixture and tip, not the factor that picks the rod.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Filler rod → Matches or complements the base metal.  
• Tip size → Controls heat input.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Rod = Right match.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Always use a rod that matches the base metal specification; the wrong rod can weaken the joint.

questions.question: What is the usual cause of runs and sags in aircraft finishes?
choices: Material is being applied too fast
Material is being applied too slow
Too much material applied in one coat
questions.answerText: Too much material applied in one coat
questions.explanation:
Runs and sags happen when too much finish is applied in one coat. The wet film is too thick to hold in place and flows downward before it dries.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Low atmospheric humidity → Low humidity speeds drying; runs are not caused by it.  
• Material is being applied too fast → A fast pass lays down a thin coat, which causes dry spray rather than runs.  
• Material is being applied too slow → A slow pass can cause a heavy coat, but the root cause is too much material, which is the keyed answer.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Runs and sags → Too much material.  
• Orange peel → Poor flow or fast drying.  
• Blushing → Moisture in humid conditions.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Heavy coat = Heavy drips.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Several light coats beat one heavy coat; this also helps control runs.

questions.question: The strength classification of fabrics used in aircraft covering is based on _____.
questions.explanation:
Aircraft covering fabric is graded by tensile strength, which is the load a strip of fabric can carry before breaking (for example Grade A versus Intermediate).  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Bearing strength → Applies to the material around fastener holes, not fabric classification.  
• Compressive strength → Fabric carries tension, not compression.  
• Shear strength → Not the basis for fabric grading.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Tensile → Pulling apart.  
• Compressive → Pushing together.  
• Shear → Sliding apart.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Fabric = Tensile.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Fabric grade tells you strength under tension, which is the main load on fabric covering.

questions.question: A female fastener with internal threads.
questions.explanation:
A nut is the female fastener with internal threads. It screws onto a bolt or stud with external threads.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Bolt → The male fastener with external threads.  
• Joggle → An offset bend in sheet metal, not a fastener.  
• Washer → A flat ring that spreads load and has no threads.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Male fastener → External threads (bolt, screw).  
• Female fastener → Internal threads (nut).  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Nut = Notch inside (threads inside).  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Know which parts are male and which are female before reading fastener questions.

questions.question: What kind of bolt has ahead symbol of asingle line?
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred, and the keyed answer (Clevis) conflicts with the standard AN bolt marking as I know it. Verify in AC 43.13-1B.  
  
On AN bolts, a single raised dash on the head marks a corrosion-resistant bolt.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Clevis → A clevis bolt is recognized by its rounded, slotted head, not by a single-line mark.  
• Low-strength material → Not a head-marking category.  
• Special → Special-purpose bolts are marked SPS, not with a single dash.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• X or asterisk → Standard steel bolt.  
• Triangle → Close-tolerance bolt.  
• Single dash → Corrosion-resistant bolt.  
• Two dashes → Aluminum alloy bolt.  
• SPS → Special-purpose bolt.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
One dash = Corrosion-resistant (CRES).  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Learn the head markings as a set; exam items usually test one against the others.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding acantilever wing?
choices: It requires only one lift strut on each side.
questions.explanation:
A cantilever wing carries its loads through internal structure (spars and ribs) attached directly to the fuselage, so no external struts or wires are needed.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Non-adjustable lift struts → Strut-braced wings use struts; cantilever wings have none.  
• Only one lift strut on each side → This describes a strut-braced wing.  
• External bracing is needed → The opposite of cantilever.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Cantilever → No external bracing.  
• Strut-braced → Uses lift struts.  
• Wire-braced → Uses flying and landing wires.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Cantilever = Can stand alone.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Cantilever wings need stronger internal spars, so they are heavier inside but cleaner aerodynamically.

questions.question: Bolt grip lengths should be _____.
choices: equal to thrice the thickness of the material to be fastened
one and one half times the thickness of the material to be fastened
equal to the length of the unthreaded portion of the bolt shank
questions.answerText: equal to the length of the unthreaded portion of the bolt shank
questions.explanation:
The grip of a bolt is its unthreaded shank length. Ideally the grip matches the thickness of the material being clamped so the threads do not bear on the material and the nut seats properly.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Diameter → A bolt's diameter is not a grip length.  
• Equal to thrice the thickness of the material → Too long; the nut would bottom out.  
• One and one half times the thickness of the material → Too long; the threads would bear on the joint.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Grip length → Unthreaded part of the shank.  
• Shank → The bolt body without head or threads.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Grip = Gripping the material with shank.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
A bolt that is slightly too long can be corrected with washers, but one that is too short cannot grip the joint.

questions.question: [Question text missing in the answer key PDF; visible fragment:] because it must be kept in cool places to retard ageing.
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: Question text is missing in the source, so this assumes it asks for the rivet alloy stored cold to retard aging.  
  
Alloy 2024 (DD rivets) hardens very quickly after heat treatment, so these rivets are kept refrigerated (ice-box rivets) to retard aging until they are driven.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 2017 → Also an ice-box rivet, but it age-hardens more slowly and is usually less strictly controlled than 2024.  
• 5056 → Not heat-treated, used on magnesium; it does not need refrigeration.  
• 7050 → A high-strength aluminum alloy used in structure, not for ice-box rivets.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• 2017 (D) → Ice-box rivet.  
• 2024 (DD) → Ice-box rivet, ages fastest.  
• 2117 (AD) → Used as received, no heat treatment needed.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
DD = Deep-freeze Drivers.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Know which rivets must be stored cold and how long after removal they can be driven.

questions.question: A naircraft grade rivet with the code MS20430DD 4-8 rivet is to be used in amilitary aircraft. The rivet head is _____.
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred, and the keyed answer (Universal) conflicts with the standard MS rivet series as I know it (MS20430 = round head). Verify before relying on it.  
  
MS20430 is the military round-head solid rivet (the replacement for AN430). In MS20430DD 4-8, DD means 2024-T31 aluminum, the diameter is 4/32 = 1/8 inch, and the length is 8/16 = 1/2 inch.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Countersunk → This is the MS20426 series.  
• Flat → This is the MS20442 series.  
• Universal → This is the MS20470 series.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• MS20426 → Countersunk.  
• MS20430 → Round.  
• MS20442 → Flat.  
• MS20470 → Universal.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
430 = Round, 470 = Universal.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Know the head type for each MS number, and read dash numbers as 32nds (diameter) and 16ths (length).

questions.question: When approaching the rear of an idling turbojet or turbofan, the hazard area extends _____ aft of the engine.
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: Published idle-power distances vary by source and engine type. This explanation follows the keyed 100 feet; verify against your reference.  
  
Behind an idling turbojet or turbofan engine, the exhaust hazard area is large because of high-velocity exhaust. The keyed answer is 100 feet, and the area grows much larger as engine power increases.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 25 feet → Far too short for an exhaust danger zone.  
• 50 feet → Still too short for a turbine engine.  
• 75 feet → Still short of the keyed distance.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Intake hazard → Suction danger in front of the engine.  
• Exhaust hazard → Heat and blast behind the engine.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Idle exhaust = Keep a long distance back, 100 ft in this key.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Danger areas grow with power. Know that the exhaust hazard is far longer than the intake hazard.

questions.question: Nickel-cadmium battery cases and drain surfaces that have been affected by electrolyte should be neutralized with _____.
questions.explanation:
Nickel-cadmium battery electrolyte is potassium hydroxide, which is alkaline. A weak acid such as boric acid neutralizes it on battery cases and drain surfaces.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Aliphatic naphtha → A cleaning solvent, not a neutralizer.  
• Aromatic naphtha → A stronger solvent used for paint removal, not a neutralizer.  
• Linseed oil → A drying oil used on wood; it does not neutralize anything.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• NiCd battery (alkaline) → Boric acid or vinegar.  
• Lead-acid battery (acid) → Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda).  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Alkaline battery = Acid cleanup (boric acid).  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Never mix up battery types or tools; using the wrong neutralizer can cause a reaction and contaminate the battery.

questions.question: The shop head of a rivet should be _____.
choices: one and one-half times the diameter of the rivet shank
one-half times the diameter of the rivet shank
one and one-half times the diameter of the manufactured head of the rivet
one-half times the diameter of the manufactured head of the rivet
questions.answerText: one and one-half times the diameter of the rivet shank
questions.explanation:
A properly formed rivet shop head is 1½ times the rivet shank diameter in width and ½ the diameter in height.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• One-half times the diameter of the rivet shank → That is the height of the shop head, not its width.  
• One and one-half times the diameter of the manufactured head → The reference is the shank diameter, not the manufactured head.  
• One-half times the diameter of the manufactured head → Wrong reference and wrong factor.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Shop head width → 1½ D.  
• Shop head height → ½ D.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
1½ wide, ½ high.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
The shop head is the head formed during driving. Know both its width and its height.

questions.question: Which fiber to resin (percent) ratio for advanced composite wet lay-ups is generally considered the best for strength?
questions.explanation:
For wet lay-ups, a fiber-to-resin ratio of about 60:40 (more fiber than resin) is generally best for strength. The fibers carry the load, and the resin only needs to hold and protect them.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 40:60 → Resin-rich, so heavy and weaker.  
• 50:50 → Better than 40:60, but still carries too much resin.  
• 70:30 → Resin-starved, with dry spots, voids, and weak bonding.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Fiber → Carries the load.  
• Resin → Holds fibers and transfers load.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
60 fiber : 40 resin.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
More resin does not mean more strength; too much resin adds weight and too little leaves dry spots.

questions.question: It is a non-electrolytic chemical treatment for aluminum alloys that increases its corrosion resistance and paint-bonding qualities.
questions.explanation:
Alodizing is a non-electrolytic chemical conversion treatment for aluminum alloys. It increases corrosion resistance and provides a good surface for paint adhesion without using electric current.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Anodizing → Uses electric current (electrolytic) to build a thicker oxide layer.  
• Dichromating → Chromate conversion treatment mainly used on magnesium.  
• Galvanizing → A zinc coating process for steel, not for aluminum.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Alodizing → Chemical, no current, aluminum.  
• Anodizing → Electrolytic, aluminum.  
• Dichromating → Chemical, magnesium.  
• Galvanizing → Zinc coating on steel.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Alodine = Aluminum, no electricity; Anodize = Applies electricity.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
The words non-electrolytic and chemical point to alodizing; electrolytic points to anodizing.

questions.question: The useful load of an aircraft is defined as the _____.
choices: difference between the maximum gross weight and empty weight
sum of the maximum gross weight and empty weight
difference between the ramp weight and weight of fuel used for ground maneuvers
difference between the maximum take-off weight and the weight of fuel used airborne
questions.answerText: difference between the maximum gross weight and empty weight
questions.explanation:
Useful load is the maximum gross weight minus the empty weight. It is what the aircraft can carry: fuel, crew, passengers, and baggage.  
  
$$W_{\text{useful}} = W_{\text{gross}} - W_{\text{empty}}$$  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Sum of the maximum gross weight and empty weight → Adding the two gives a meaningless number.  
• Difference between the ramp weight and the weight of fuel used for ground maneuvers → This gives takeoff weight, not useful load.  
• Difference between maximum take-off weight and fuel used airborne → This approximates landing weight.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Empty weight → Aircraft structure and fixed equipment.  
• Useful load → What you can add.  
• Gross weight → Total aircraft weight.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Useful = Max minus Empty.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Useful load includes fuel, crew, passengers, and baggage.

questions.question: The minimum grain count for softwoods is _____.
questions.explanation:
The minimum grain count for softwoods such as spruce is six annual rings per inch. Fewer rings indicate coarse, weaker wood.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Eight rings per inch → Acceptable, but not the minimum.  
• Twelve rings per inch → Acceptable, but not the minimum.  
• Sixteen rings per inch → Acceptable, but not the minimum.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Grain count → Rings per inch.  
• Slope of grain → Maximum allowed is 1:15.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Six rings per inch minimum.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Higher ring counts are fine; the exam asks for the minimum.

questions.question: The smallest allowable edge distance is _____.
questions.explanation:
The smallest allowable edge distance is 2D (twice the rivet diameter), measured from the center of the rivet hole to the edge of the sheet.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 3D → The minimum rivet pitch, not the edge distance.  
• 4D → The maximum edge distance.  
• 12D → The maximum rivet pitch.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Edge distance → 2D minimum, 4D maximum.  
• Rivet pitch → 3D minimum, 12D maximum.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Edge 2D, Pitch 3D.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Memorize the four numbers (2D, 4D, 3D, 12D) and what each applies to.

questions.question: The testing medium that is generally used in magnetic particle inspection utilizes aferromagnetic material that has _____.
questions.explanation:
Magnetic-particle inspection uses ferromagnetic particles with high permeability (easily magnetized) and low retentivity (they do not stay magnetized). They gather at flux leakage from cracks without clumping on the background.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• High permeability and high retentivity → Particles stay magnetized and cling to each other and the surface, giving false indications.  
• Low permeability and high retentivity → They respond poorly and stay magnetized.  
• Low permeability and low retentivity → They respond poorly to the magnetic field.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Permeability → How easily a material is magnetized.  
• Retentivity → How well it stays magnetized.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Particles = Pick up easily, let go easily.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Remember to demagnetize the part after inspection.

questions.question: Aircraft bolts are usually manufactured with a _____ for the threads.
questions.explanation:
⚠️ Answer key check: This answer was inferred, and the keyed answer (Free fit) conflicts with what I recall (Class 3, medium fit). Please verify in your reference.  
  
Class 3 (medium fit) is commonly cited for aircraft bolt threads, giving a snug but easy-to-assemble fit that resists loosening and still allows quick installation.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Free fit → Class 2, a general-purpose fit.  
• Interference fit → Not used for threads; this describes press-fitted parts.  
• Loose fit → Class 1, the loosest fit.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Class 1 → Loose fit.  
• Class 2 → Free fit.  
• Class 3 → Medium fit.  
• Class 4 → Close fit.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Class 3 = Medium, mid-aircraft grade.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Know the four thread fit classes in order of tightness.

questions.question: What load causes most rivet failures?
questions.explanation:
Rivets are designed to carry shear loads (forces trying to slide the joined sheets past each other). Shear is the load most likely to cause rivet failure, and rivets should not carry tension.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Bearing → Failure occurs in the sheet around the hole, not in the rivet.  
• Bending → Not a typical rivet failure load.  
• Compression → Not a typical rivet failure load.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Shear → Sliding load.  
• Bearing → Crushing at the hole edge.  
• Tension → Pulling load.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Rivets Rip sideways (shear).  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Rivets are strong in shear and weak in tension; design joints so they work in shear.

questions.question: Alloy within the _____ utilize Magnesium as the principal alloying agent; alloy within the _____ utilize Manganese as the principal alloying agent.
questions.explanation:
In aluminum alloy designations, the 5000 series uses magnesium as the principal alloying agent, and the 3000 series uses manganese.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• 3000 series; 5000 series → Reversed.  
• 3000 series; 4000 series → 3000 is manganese, and 4000 is silicon.  
• 5000 series; 4000 series → 5000 is magnesium, and 4000 is silicon, not manganese.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• 1xxx → Pure aluminum.  
• 2xxx → Copper.  
• 3xxx → Manganese.  
• 4xxx → Silicon.  
• 5xxx → Magnesium.  
• 6xxx → Magnesium and silicon.  
• 7xxx → Zinc.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
3 = Manganese, 5 = Magnesium.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Know the full series list; the exam often tests several at once.

questions.question: A particular component is attached to the aircraft structure by the use of an aircraft bolt and acastle tension nut combination. If the cotter pin hole does not align with the recommended torque range, the acceptable practice is to _____.
choices: let it be because it is anormal practice
change the washers and try again
exceed the maximum recommended torque range by no more than 10%
questions.answerText: change the washers and try again
questions.explanation:
If the cotter pin hole does not align within the allowed torque range, change the washer (use a thicker or thinner AN960) and try again. This keeps the torque within limits while allowing the cotter pin to be installed.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Tighten below the torque range → Under-torque risks a loose joint.  
• Let it be because it is a normal practice → Without the cotter pin the nut is not secured.  
• Exceed the maximum recommended torque by no more than 10% → Over-torque can overstress the bolt, so it is not the preferred fix.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Castle nut → Slots for a cotter pin.  
• Torque range → Preload limits that must stay within spec.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
No hole match? Switch the washer.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Shift alignment with washers and keep the torque in range.

questions.question: Aircraft bolts with a cross or asterisk on the bolt head are _____.
questions.explanation:
Aircraft bolts marked with a cross (X) or an asterisk on the head are standard steel AN bolts.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Close-tolerance bolts → Marked with a triangle.  
• Made of aluminum alloy → Marked with two raised dashes.  
• Magnetically inspected → A process step, not what the cross or asterisk shows.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• X or asterisk → Standard steel bolt.  
• Triangle → Close-tolerance bolt.  
• Single dash → Corrosion-resistant.  
• Two dashes → Aluminum alloy.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
X marks the standard steel spot.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Head markings are tested often; learn them as a set.

questions.question: Statement 1: The installation of permanent ballast results in adecrease in the aircraft empty wei ght and an increase in the useful load. Statement 2: A permanent ballast remains in the aircraft for a long period of time.
choices: Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct.
questions.answerText: Statement 1 is incorrect; Statement 2 is correct.
questions.explanation:
Permanent ballast is added weight installed to keep the CG within limits, and it stays in the aircraft for the long term. That makes Statement 2 correct. Statement 1 is wrong because ballast increases the empty weight, and with a fixed gross weight the useful load decreases.  
  
$$W_{\text{useful}} = W_{\text{gross}} - W_{\text{empty}}$$  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Both statements are correct → Statement 1 reverses the effect on empty weight and useful load.  
• Both statements are incorrect → Statement 2 is correct.  
• Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect → Reversed; Statement 2 is correct and Statement 1 is wrong.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Permanent ballast → Stays installed; counts in empty weight.  
• Temporary ballast → Removable; used for loading adjustments.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Ballast adds to empty weight, so useful load drops.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Any change to empty weight changes useful load by the opposite amount.

questions.question: In selecting a torch tip size to be used in welding, the size of the tip opening determines _____.
choices: melting point of the filler material
amount of heat applied to work
questions.answerText: amount of heat applied to work
questions.explanation:
The torch tip opening size controls how much gas flows, and so how much heat is delivered to the work. A larger tip gives more heat and is used for thicker material.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Material compatibility → Depends on rod and base metal, not the tip.  
• Temperature of the flame → Set by the gas type and mixture, not the tip size.  
• Melting point of the filler material → A property of the filler rod.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Tip size → Quantity of heat.  
• Gas mixture → Flame temperature.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Big tip = Big heat quantity.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Match the tip to the metal thickness, as too much heat burns through and too little gives poor fusion.

questions.question: What is the location of the center of gravity in %MAC if the center of gravity is 295 inches from the datum, LEMAC is 270 inches from the datum, root chord is 70 inches, and tip chord is 35 inches?
questions.explanation:
For a tapered wing, first find the mean aerodynamic chord (MAC), then the CG position as a percentage of it.  
  
$$MAC = \frac{2}{3}\left(C_r + C_t - \frac{C_r C_t}{C_r + C_t}\right) = \frac{2}{3}\left(70 + 35 - \frac{70 \times 35}{105}\right) \approx 54.4\ \text{in}$$  
  
$$\%MAC = \frac{CG - LEMAC}{MAC} \times 100 = \frac{295 - 270}{54.4} \times 100 \approx 45.9\%$$  
  
That falls between 45 and 48.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Between 39 and 42 → Result of using a wrong MAC.  
• Between 42 and 45 → Result of an arithmetic slip.  
• Between 48 and 51 → Result of an arithmetic slip.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• LEMAC → Leading edge of the MAC.  
• %MAC → CG position along the MAC.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Subtract LEMAC from CG, then divide by MAC.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Always compute MAC first for a tapered wing; averaging the chords is only an approximation.

questions.question: One of the purposes of the ailerons is to provide stability about the _____.
questions.explanation:
Ailerons control roll about the longitudinal axis, which is lateral stability and control.  
  
Why the other choices are incorrect:  
• Directional stability → Yaw about the vertical axis, handled by the rudder and vertical fin.  
• Longitudinal stability → Pitch about the lateral axis, handled by the elevator and horizontal stabilizer.  
• Horizontal stability → Not a standard stability term.  
  
Differentiate Similar Concepts:  
• Ailerons → Roll → Lateral.  
• Elevator → Pitch → Longitudinal.  
• Rudder → Yaw → Directional.  
  
💡 Memory Hook:  
Ailerons = Roll = Lateral.  
  
🎯 Board Tip:  
Match each control surface to its axis and its type of stability.
